name: opensysml-sysml
description: SysML v2 and KerML syntax highlighting and language support backed by the OpenSysML language server.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode the language server is only started from `opensysml.server.path` or `PATH`, never from the workspace's own `bin/` directory, and the server settings are read from user settings only.

opensysml.server.path.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `sysml-lsp` executable. When empty, `sysml-lsp` is looked up on `PATH`.

opensysml.server.args.description: Extra arguments passed to the language server.

opensysml.server.enabled.description: Start the language server. Turn this off to keep syntax highlighting only.

opensysml.trace.server.description: Trace the communication with the language server.

opensysml.diagram.autoOpen.markdownDescription: Open the diagram of a SysML or KerML file beside its editor as soon as the file is shown. A diagram you close stays closed for that file until you run **SysML: Open Diagram** on it again.

enumDescriptions: Follow the VS Code colour theme.
The pilot visualizer's Standard B&W: white canvas, black text, thin dark borders, square definitions and rounded usages.
Cameo Systems Modeler's look: 11px Arial, pale-yellow gradient fills with thin dark borders, and a DOT export drawn in the server's cameo style.
The pilot look, filled by keyword family from the Okabe–Ito palette.
The pilot look, filled by keyword family from Paul Tol's bright palette.
The pilot look, filled by keyword family from Paul Tol's muted palette.
The pilot look, filled by keyword family from Paul Tol's light palette.
The pilot look, filled by keyword family from ColorBrewer Set2.
The pilot look, filled by keyword family from ColorBrewer Dark2.
The pilot look, filled by keyword family from the viridis colour map.
The pilot look, filled by keyword family from the cividis colour map.
opensysml.diagram.style.markdownDescription: The look every diagram is drawn in, also chosen from the **Style** list in the diagram panel. A palette colours definitions with their keyword family's colour and usages with a lighter tint of it, the same colours the DOT and PlantUML exports take; text stays black. `cameo` draws Cameo Systems Modeler's look and asks the server for its cameo drawing style when the diagram is exported as DOT.

enumDescriptions: A case's actor, subject and stakeholder parameters and an action's parameter pins as symbols on the node's boundary; without them a connection ends at the node itself.
A part's ports as symbols on its boundary; without them a connection ends at the part.
The compartments listing a node's nested features.
The names of connections, flows and bindings along their lines.
The «keyword» over each name.
Multiplicities after names.
The `: Type` after a name.
The qualified-name prefix of each name.
Every optional notation element.

opensysml.diagram.show.markdownDescription: Optional notation elements every diagram draws besides the ones its view's rendering shows and the default (port symbols, compartments and keywords), by the names the SysML v2 notation makes optional; `all` draws every one. Applies to the diagram panel and to exports, on a server that lists the elements (`openSysmlRenderElements`).

enumDescriptions: Open the diagram in the group beside its source editor.
Move the diagram out into a floating window of its own as soon as it opens.
opensysml.diagram.openIn.markdownDescription: Where the first diagram panel opens. Later diagrams join the group the open one is in, a floating window's included; **SysML: Move Diagram to New Window** moves an open diagram at any time.

enumDescriptions: Draw an edge along the `Route` its view states, and route only the edges without one.

Route every edge the automatic layout did not, including those with a stated `Route`, orthogonally around the boxes. The stated routes stay in the model but are not drawn, and the waypoint handles are hidden.
opensysml.diagram.routing.markdownDescription: Whose routes the diagram panel draws its edges along. This is a drawing setting of the panel only: `sysml -render-lines` and the diagram exports keep drawing the stated routes.

opensysml.diagram.hideRelations.markdownDescription: Relationship kinds the diagram panel hides by default, by the kind names the rendering's edges carry (for example `typing`, `specialization`, `composition`). Each panel's **Relations** list shows the kinds present in its diagram and overrides this for that panel alone; nothing is written to the model, and exports are unaffected.

opensysml.diagram.depth.markdownDescription: How many levels of nested elements a tree or interconnection diagram draws below each exposed element, overriding the `depth` the view states; `0` draws every level the view allows. Applies to the diagram panel and to exports, on a server that reads a depth (`openSysmlRenderDepth`).

element.description: Qualified name of the element a Run or Evaluate code lens checks.

keybindings.when: editorTextFocus && (editorLangId == sysml || editorLangId == kerml) || activeWebviewPanelId == opensysml.diagram
editorTextFocus && (editorLangId == sysml || editorLangId == kerml) || activeWebviewPanelId == opensysml.diagram

editor/title.when: resourceLangId == sysml || resourceLangId == kerml || activeWebviewPanelId == opensysml.diagram

scripts.typecheck: tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p src/webview/tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p src/landing/tsconfig.json
scripts.package: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build -- --production && vsce package --no-dependencies --out opensysml-sysml.vsix
